validated_results.title: Calcium, dairy products, and risk of prostate cancer in a prospective cohort of United States men.
validated_results.journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
validated_results.reason: Prospective cohort of US men reporting multivariate-adjusted rate ratios for total and dietary calcium intake and incident prostate cancer.

extraction.comparison_type: >=2000 versus <700 mg/day of total calcium intake (diet and supplements)
extraction.population: Elderly United States men in the Cancer Prevention Study II Nutrition Cohort

sample_size.excerpt: After excluding men with a history of cancer or incomplete dietary information, 65,321 men remained for analysis. During follow-up through August 31, 1999, we documented 3811 cases of incident prostate cancer.

cases.excerpt: During follow-up through August 31, 1999, we documented 3811 cases of incident prostate cancer.

effect_size.excerpt: Total calcium intake (from diet and supplements) was associated with modestly increased risk of prostate cancer [RR = 1.2, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.0-1.6 for >or=2000 versus <700 mg/day, P trend = 0.02).
